decisions.quote:
This study presents a replication and extension of the original study (Spadini et al.
2018) by examining a broader range of projects on GitHub, the most representative
platform of the PR review model. The results for RQ1 confirm that reviewers primar-
ily focus on production code, though this tendency is somewhat mitigated on GitHub
compared to other platforms.

decisions.reason: Under the codebook, confirming one tested effect is a single comparison rather than an overall replication verdict, and when a paper reports some findings as agreeing with the original study while explicitly marking others as differing from the original, the outcome is mixed. Here, the authors confirm Spadini et al. (2018) on reviewers primarily focusing on production code in mixed PRs (RQ1 Scenario A) and reviewing production code before test code (RQ3, 74.33%), but explicitly contrast their findings with the original study on overall attention balance and Scenario B odds ratios (RQ1) as well as test review discussion topics (RQ2, where GitHub reviewers focus much more on superficial code improvements and less on defect detection and comprehension than in Gerrit). Parent primary-source confirmation: Primary Discussion confirms the original production-first review finding, while Introduction/Results explicitly contrast GitHub versus original Gerrit review balance and test-discussion topics. The newly studied GHA temporal effect is an extension, not itself a failed original finding; the platform-specific original comparisons nevertheless contain both agreement and disagreement, supporting mixed.

prior_decision.quote: The goal of this work is to replicate and extend the work by Spadini et al. (Spadini et al. 2018) (referred to as the “original study” ). First, our empirical study replicates the original study ’s quantitative and qualitative analyses using the GitHub PR review model. Furthermore, we extend their research by examining how the introduction of GHA affects reviewer and developer practices regarding test code. Our findings reveal notable differences from the original study, reflecting the evolving dynamics of code review models and testing practices in the era of integrated CI tools such as GHA.
